report:
The article satisfies every completion criterion under its explicitly stated sufficient conditions. No substantial repair is needed. The residual positivity and selector bounds are antecedents of the theorem, not assumptions granted by the original task; the product constructions establish that these antecedents hold for a nonempty family of genuinely non-descended selectors.

Holomorphic descent is valid: coefficients are constant on compact connected fibers, and local holomorphic right inverses of the submersion make the descended coefficients holomorphic. Smooth local norms and positive volume densities preserve integrability, so the section spaces retain the task’s norm-independent meaning.

The anisotropic integral is correct. Polar coordinates give exponents α₀=(ℓ+1)/p and αⱼ=1/bⱼ. Simplex radial integration reduces convergence to ∫ρ^{Σαⱼ−P−1}dρ. Thus convergence requires Σαⱼ>P, with logarithmic divergence at equality. Taking P=mc/p gives ℓ+1>mc−a, where a=pΣ1/bⱼ, and hence K_m=max{0,⌊mc−a⌋}. Auxiliary variables, bounded errors and holomorphic units preserve this threshold.

Both dimension proofs were checked independently. In the submean proof, an affine holomorphic frame change removes the constant and linear metric terms; the remaining weight is uniformly bounded on balls of radius N^{-1/2}. Evaluation therefore has squared norm O(N^s). Because its target is one-dimensional, this bounds the sum over an orthonormal basis without an extra dimension factor. Integration proves h⁰=O(N^s). The alternative jet proof also closes: finite chains of three-radius estimates give μ≥e^{-CN}M, while vanishing of order k gives μ≤e^{CN}2^{-k}M, so jets of order O(N) are injective. Divisor restriction sequences then bound each layer by O(m^{q−1}); no restriction surjectivity or cohomology vanishing is assumed.

With the task’s normalization, Poincaré–Lelong gives θ+ddᶜψ=β+c[D]. This is positive and closed. Its non-pluripolar product equals β^q off D and assigns no mass to D, hence equals β^q globally. Compactness makes its mass finite, and strict positivity of β makes it positive. The argument includes q=1. The normalization follows directly from the operator and inverse-norm formula in [Andersson](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0412446); the non-pluripolar application matches [BEGZ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674).

The base ideal formula I(mψ)=O(−⌊mc⌋D) is correct for arbitrary germs, including germs whose leading coefficient vanishes at the chart center: a nonzero leading coefficient is nonzero on a nearby open set of tangential coordinates, where insufficient divisor order causes divergence. Global domination gives φ≥π*ψ−C'', and Fubini in submersion charts proves W_m⊂V_m for every positive integer m.

For the reverse bound, a smooth connected divisor is irreducible. A nonzero section’s leading divisorial coefficient cannot vanish identically throughout the witness chart, by the identity theorem on D. Shrinking around a point where it is nonzero yields a unit coefficient and permits application of the anisotropic integral. Consequently V_m⊂H⁰(A^m(−K_mD)). The zero section is automatic. Since 0≤L_m−K_m≤⌈a⌉, the restriction estimate proves the claimed O(m^{q−1})=o(m^q) defect. For q=1, D is one reduced point and each layer costs at most one dimension, giving the stated bound by ⌈a⌉.

The exact-model corollary establishes both inclusions. Compactness and the bounded-error models give the global lower bound; local boundedness outside Z excludes further constraints. Sections divisible by z^{K_m} are integrable in every pole chart because K_m+1>mc−a. Thus the exact description of V_m holds for every m.

The examples are admissible. Locally, Q is a sum of squared holomorphic coefficients with smooth positive metric factors. Adding a sufficiently positive quadratic function makes log Q plurisubharmonic away from its common zero locus; the locally bounded-above extension theorem applies across that proper analytic locus. A finite covering gives ddᶜlog Q≥−C₀ω. Small positive λ therefore ensures ω-plurisubharmonicity. An ample bundle admits a positive smooth metric, and its smooth comparison with the prescribed h supplies u; sufficiently small c=pλ also makes β positive. Both restrictions can be imposed simultaneously. These applications match [Demailly’s ample-metric construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9410022) and [extension theorem](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf). The additional residual-class equivalence in n2 correctly uses the compact Kähler ddᶜ lemma, with u=2πϕ in [Tosatti’s normalization](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.04823).

The product poles meet a nonempty proper subset of every fiber over D and are finite elsewhere on that fiber. This rules out pullback singularity type even modulo bounded functions. Taking B=P^q, A=O(1) and D a hyperplane supplies examples in every q≥1. In the explicit p=2, b₁=3 example, K₁=L₁=0 and K_m=L_m−1 for every m≥2. Monomial counting gives exactly binom(⌈m/2⌉+q,q−1), with the claimed asymptotic and defect one when q=1.

The [cited monograph](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Papers/SHPT_vibe.pdf) confirms the isotropic theorem and sharp example. Independently, p=bⱼ=1 and r=f recover K_m=max{⌊mc⌋−f,0}. Unequal powers, unused fiber directions and the single-chart witness extend that scope. The sufficient features are precisely the controlled horizontal slope, a divisorial witness over an open part of connected D, finite transverse integrability gain, and global exclusion of stronger constraints. No universal existence or necessary-and-sufficient classification follows or is claimed. The zero-dimensional-fiber case and trivial-bundle obstruction are correctly qualified.

Two harmless wording clarifications: when mc−a=0, the failing order −1 mentioned in auxiliary endpoint wording is only formal; the minimum admissible order is zero. In the Fubini–Study example, take u with θ+ddᶜu=ω_B when the prescribed h is arbitrary. Neither clarification changes a conclusion. Prior PASS flags, acceptance records and the failed authentication call provide no mathematical evidence for this audit.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold Y, every smooth real d-exact (1,1)-form γ is dd^c u for some smooth real function u, with dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂.

An ample holomorphic line bundle L on a compact complex manifold Y, where ample means that some positive tensor power is very ample, admits a smooth Hermitian metric whose Chern curvature c_1(L,H) is a Kähler form.
passages.quote: every ample line bundle F has a smooth hermitian metric with positive definite curvature form

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold Y of dimension q≥1, the non-pluripolar top product of a positive closed (1,1)-current T is well-defined, assigns zero mass to pluripolar sets, and agrees with T^q on every open subset where T is smooth. In degree one, for a local plurisubharmonic potential v, ⟨dd^c v⟩=1_{v>−∞}dd^c v.

passages.statement: Xia’s working manuscript, Theorem 26.10.1, gives this isotropic result: let π:X→B be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected compact complex manifolds with connected f-dimensional fibers, f≥1, and Kähler base of dimension q≥1. Let A have smooth positive curvature θ, let D be a nonempty smooth divisor admitting a holomorphic section σ:D→X, and assume β=θ−cη>0, where c>0 and η=c_1(O(D),H_D). If φ∈PSH(X,ω) is locally bounded off σ(D) and equals c log(|z|²+Σ_{j=1}^f|w_j|²)+O(1) there in adapted coordinates, then ψ=c log||s_D||² has non-pluripolar product β^q. For every m≥1, V_m=H⁰(B,A^m(−max{⌊mc⌋−f,0}D)), W_m=H⁰(B,A^m(−⌊mc⌋D))⊂V_m, and the defect is O(m^{q−1}). Example 26.10.1 attains this order, including positive eventual constant defect for q=1.
passages.quote: The function 𝜓 is 𝜃-plurisubharmonic, with positive non-pluripolar mass
